sections.name: View
sections.description:
View constructs a retained container from children. Configure it with fluent
properties, events, and styles. Apply reusable styles with Element.Style.

sections.name: Checkbox
sections.signature: pub fn new(state: impl Into<ToggleState>) -> Self

entries.name: parent
entries.type: pub fn parent(children: impl IntoIterator<Item = bool>) -> Self
entries.description: Derive a parent checkbox from the checked values of the boxes it governs. This is Base UI's `parent` checkbox: every child checked reports on, none reports off, and a mix reports mixed. QuickGUI keeps no child registry — the application passes the values it is already rendering — so the derivation stays a pure function of the caller's own data. ``` use quickgui::{Checkbox, ToggleState}; assert_eq!(Checkbox::parent([true, true]).state(), ToggleState::On); assert_eq!(Checkbox::parent([false, false]).state(), ToggleState::Off); assert_eq!(Checkbox::parent([true, false]).state(), ToggleState::Mixed); // An empty group is unchecked rather than mixed. assert_eq!(Checkbox::parent([]).state(), ToggleState::Off); ```

entries.name: read_only
entries.type: pub const fn read_only(mut self, read_only: bool) -> Self
entries.description: Show a value the user may read but not change, Base UI's `readOnly`. Unlike a disabled checkbox, a read-only one stays focusable and stays in the Tab sequence. QuickGUI projects the state and refuses the transition through [`Self::next_state`]; the application's own listener asks for that transition rather than toggling blindly.

entries.name: state
entries.description: Configures state for this part.

entries.name: is_read_only
entries.description: Configures is read only for this part.

entries.name: next_state
entries.description: The state an activation moves this checkbox to, or `None` when it refuses. Mixed and off both move to on, and on moves to off, which is the web's tri-state contract. A read-only checkbox returns `None`, so a click listener that asks before writing cannot change a value the control is refusing.

entries.name: parent_next_checked
entries.description: The checked value activating a parent checkbox moves its whole group to. A partially or fully unchecked parent checks everything; a fully checked one clears it. Returns `None` when the parent is read-only.

sections.description: Create an unstyled controlled checkbox root. This shorthand is equivalent to `Checkbox::new(state).root_part(div())`. Use [`Checkbox`] directly when composing a separate indicator part.

sections.name: CheckboxGroup::root_part
sections.signature: pub fn root_part(self, root: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate an application-owned group root without adding layout or appearance. Pair it with a [`crate::Field`] label, or with [`crate::Element::accessibility_labelled_by`], to name the group.

sections.name: CheckboxGroup::checkbox_part
sections.signature: pub fn checkbox_part(self, value: impl Into<ElementId>, checkbox: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate one application-owned checkbox for `value`. The part reuses the existing [`Checkbox`] descriptor, so the checkbox role, exact on/off/mixed semantics, click behavior, and desktop pointer contract are identical to a standalone checkbox. A disabled group disables every item.

sections.name: CheckboxGroup::indicator_part
sections.signature: pub fn indicator_part(self, indicator: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Hide an application-owned indicator inside one item from the accessible name.

sections.name: CheckboxGroup::parent_part
sections.signature: pub fn parent_part(self, parent: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the application-owned parent checkbox. Its checked state is derived: on when every declared value is checked, mixed when only some are, and off when none are. QuickGUI retains no separate parent value, so the parent can never disagree with its children.

entries.name: display_value
entries.description: Format every thumb value into one string for a caller-owned value part. This is Base UI's Root `format` prop applied through the shared [`crate::ValueFormat`]. A range slider joins its thumbs with an en dash, which is the shape Base UI's Value renders by default.

entries.name: thumb
entries.type: pub fn thumb(self, index: usize) -> Option<SliderThumb>
entries.description: Describe one thumb. Indices at or past [`SliderState::thumb_count`] return `None` so a caller-driven loop stays bounded by the state instead of by its own arithmetic.

sections.name: Slider::root_part
sections.signature: pub fn root_part(self, root: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate an application-owned root without adding layout or appearance. A single-thumb slider becomes the focusable Slider itself. Pair it with [`Self::key_part`] to attach the typed keyboard actions.

sections.name: Slider::key_part
sections.signature: pub fn key_part<V: 'static>( self, cx: &mut ViewContext<'_, V>, root: Element, access: fn(&mut V) -> &mut SliderState, ) -> Element
sections.description: Attach QuickGUI's typed slider keyboard actions to a single-thumb root. Install [`slider_key_bindings`] once on the application keymap. Multi-thumb sliders use [`SliderThumb::key_part`] instead so each thumb owns its own focus.

sections.name: Slider::track_part
sections.signature: pub fn track_part(self, track: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate an application-owned track. Base UI uses [`Self::control_part`] as the larger interactive surface. A declaration that omits Control can keep the earlier behavior by attaching a [`crate::ViewContext::pointer_listener`] registered for [`Self::track_id`] and forwarding the event to [`SliderState::apply_pointer`] with the size the caller laid out.

sections.name: Slider::range_part
sections.signature: pub fn range_part(self, range: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the application-owned fill between the slider's minimum and its value.

sections.name: Slider::indicator_part
sections.signature: pub fn indicator_part(self, indicator: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Base UI's Indicator name for the filled part of the track. This is the same decorator as [`Self::range_part`]; both names stay supported.

sections.name: Slider::control_part
sections.signature: pub fn control_part(self, control: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the caller-owned interactive area that carries the slider's pointer capture. Base UI separates the Control — the region a press acts on — from the Track it paints. Attach a [`crate::ViewContext::pointer_listener`] registered for [`Self::control_id`] and forward the event to [`SliderState::apply_pointer_change`] with the size the caller laid out. A caller that omits this part can keep pointer capture on [`Self::track_part`].

sections.name: Slider::label_part
sections.signature: pub fn label_part(self, label: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Assign the stable mounted label target the slider points at. A single-thumb slider takes its accessible name from this part. A multi-thumb slider names its group from it, and each thumb still needs its own accessible name.

sections.name: Slider::value_part
sections.signature: pub fn value_part(self, value: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Assign the stable mounted value target the slider points at. Put [`Self::display_value`] inside it; QuickGUI never renders the text itself.

entries.description: The inclusive bounds this thumb may move between, honoring its neighbors.

entries.name: fraction
entries.description: The `0.0..=1.0` position of this thumb along the track.

entries.description: Configures is active for this part.

entries.name: thumb_id
entries.description: Configures thumb id for this part.

entries.description: Whether a captured pointer is currently dragging this slider, Base UI's `data-dragging`.

entries.name: state
entries.description: A copyable render-state snapshot the application styles this thumb from.

entries.name: offset
entries.type: pub fn offset(self, track_length: f32, thumb_length: f32) -> f32
entries.description: The leading-edge offset of this thumb along the track, honoring the thumb alignment. `track_length` and `thumb_length` are measured along the slider's own axis. This is the one place Base UI's `thumbAlignment` changes anything: `Center` lets the thumb overhang both ends, `Edge` keeps its box inside the track.

entries.name: value_text
entries.description: Format this thumb's value, Base UI's Thumb `getAriaValueText` equivalent. Pass the result to `Element::accessibility_value` on the thumb; QuickGUI never renders it.

entries.name: key_part_with
entries.type: pub fn key_part_with<V: 'static>( self, cx: &mut ViewContext<'_, V>, thumb: Element, access: StateAccessor<V, SliderState>, ) -> Element
entries.description: Attach this thumb's typed keyboard actions against a per-instance state accessor.

sections.name: SliderThumb::thumb_part
sections.signature: pub fn thumb_part(self, thumb: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate an application-owned thumb without adding layout or appearance. A single-thumb slider keeps its value on the root, so its thumb is decorative and hidden from assistive technology. Every thumb of a multi-thumb slider is an independently focusable Slider bounded by its neighbors.

sections.name: SliderThumb::key_part
sections.signature: pub fn key_part<V: 'static>( self, cx: &mut ViewContext<'_, V>, thumb: Element, access: fn(&mut V) -> &mut SliderState, ) -> Element
sections.description: Attach QuickGUI's typed slider keyboard actions to this thumb. Focusing the thumb also makes it the active thumb, so arrows move the thumb the user sees.

sections.name: NumberField::root_part
sections.signature: pub fn root_part(self, root: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate an application-owned root without adding layout or appearance.

sections.name: NumberField::input_part
sections.signature: pub fn input_part(self, state: &NumberFieldState, input: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the application-owned controlled input. Pass a [`crate::text_input`] built from [`NumberFieldState::text`] with the caller's own [`crate::Element::on_input`] listener. QuickGUI adds the spin-button semantics: the committed numeric value, the field's bounds and step, and invalid state.

sections.name: NumberField::increment_part
sections.signature: pub fn increment_part(self, state: &NumberFieldState, increment: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the application-owned increment button. Steppers stay out of the Tab sequence because the input already answers arrow keys, which matches native desktop spin buttons.

sections.name: NumberField::decrement_part
sections.signature: pub fn decrement_part(self, state: &NumberFieldState, decrement: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the application-owned decrement button.

sections.name: NumberField::group_part
sections.signature: pub fn group_part(self, group: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the caller-owned group that wraps the decrement, input, and increment parts. Base UI's Group keeps the three controls one addressable unit; QuickGUI supplies the stable identity and the Group role and adds no layout, so the application still chooses the row, the order, and the spacing.

sections.name: NumberField::scrub_area_part
sections.signature: pub fn scrub_area_part(self, state: &NumberFieldState, scrub_area: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the caller-owned area a pointer drag scrubs the value over. Attach a [`crate::ViewContext::pointer_listener`] registered for [`Self::scrub_area_id`] and forward the event to [`NumberFieldState::apply_scrub`]. QuickGUI supplies the identity, the axis-appropriate resize cursor, drag exclusion, and text-selection suppression; the area is hidden from assistive technology because the input already carries the spin-button semantics.

sections.name: NumberField::scrub_area_cursor_part
sections.signature: pub fn scrub_area_cursor_part(self, cursor: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the caller-owned cursor a scrub area shows while it is being dragged. Mount it only while [`NumberFieldState::is_scrubbing`] is true and place it from [`NumberFieldState::scrub_position`]; QuickGUI supplies the identity and keeps the decoration out of the accessible name and out of hit testing.

sections.name: SelectState::label_part
sections.signature: pub fn label_part(id: impl Into<ElementId>, label: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the caller-owned visible label, Base UI's `Select.Label`. [`Self::trigger_part`] points at this identity, so the label names the control without its text being copied into a second accessible string.

sections.name: SelectState::value_part
sections.signature: pub fn value_part(id: impl Into<ElementId>, value: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the caller-owned value text inside the trigger, Base UI's `Select.Value`. The trigger already exposes the selected value, so this part is hidden from assistive technology and would otherwise be announced twice. Render [`Self::value_text`] inside it, or the placeholder when it returns `None`.

sections.name: SelectState::icon_part
sections.signature: pub fn icon_part(id: impl Into<ElementId>, icon: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the caller-owned trigger affordance, Base UI's `Select.Icon`.

sections.name: SelectState::backdrop_part
sections.signature: pub fn backdrop_part(id: impl Into<ElementId>, backdrop: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate an optional caller-painted owner-window backdrop, Base UI's `Select.Backdrop`. The option surface is a separate native child window that already takes the pointer grab, so this layer exists only for a caller-painted dimming pass. Mount it while [`Self::is_open`] is true, and declare [`Self::modal`] so the intent is inspectable.

sections.name: SelectState::portal_part
sections.signature: pub fn portal_part( id: impl Into<ElementId>, label: impl Into<Arc<str>>, option_count: usize, multiple: bool, portal: Element, ) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the popup boundary, Base UI's `Select.Portal` and `Select.Positioner`. QuickGUI's option surface is its own native window, so the portal, the positioner, and the popup are one element: all three names decorate it identically and QuickGUI resolves its placement against the display work area rather than a parent stacking context.

sections.name: SelectState::positioner_part
sections.signature: pub fn positioner_part( id: impl Into<ElementId>, label: impl Into<Arc<str>>, option_count: usize, multiple: bool, positioner: Element, ) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the popup boundary, Base UI's `Select.Positioner`.

sections.name: SelectState::popup_part
sections.signature: pub fn popup_part( id: impl Into<ElementId>, label: impl Into<Arc<str>>, option_count: usize, multiple: bool, popup: Element, ) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the caller-owned option surface, Base UI's `Select.Popup`. QuickGUI applies this to whatever the surface renderer returns, so an application that composes its own in-window list can reuse exactly the semantics the native surface gets.

sections.name: SelectState::arrow_part
sections.signature: pub fn arrow_part(id: impl Into<ElementId>, arrow: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Position a caller-owned decorative arrow, Base UI's `Select.Arrow`.

sections.name: SelectState::list_part
sections.signature: pub fn list_part(id: impl Into<ElementId>, option_count: usize, list: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the caller-owned scrolling option list, Base UI's `Select.List`. The popup already carries the list-box role, so the inner list is a structural container: it keeps a stable identity and the declared set size without announcing a second list.

sections.name: SelectState::item_part
sections.signature: pub fn item_part( row_id: impl Into<ElementId>, label: impl Into<Arc<str>>, state: SelectOptionState, row: Element, ) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate one caller-owned option row, Base UI's `Select.Item`. `row_id` comes from [`Self::option_id_for_source`], so the row keeps the identity the popup's active-descendant relationship points at.

sections.name: SelectState::item_text_part
sections.description: Decorate one option's visible text, Base UI's `Select.ItemText`. The row already carries the accessible name, so the text is decoration.

sections.name: SelectState::item_indicator_part
sections.description: Decorate one option's selected mark, Base UI's `Select.ItemIndicator`. The row already reports selection, so the indicator is hidden from assistive technology. Mount it only while the row is selected, exactly as Base UI does.

sections.name: SelectState::group_part
sections.description: Decorate a caller-composed option group, Base UI's `Select.Group`.

sections.name: SelectState::group_label_part
sections.signature: pub fn group_label_part(label_id: impl Into<ElementId>, label: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate a group's visible label, Base UI's `Select.GroupLabel`. Pass the same `label_id` to [`Element::accessibility_labelled_by`] on the group so the two are related without the text being copied.

sections.name: SelectState::separator_part
sections.description: Decorate a caller-owned divider between option groups, Base UI's `Select.Separator`.

entries.description: Set the initial free-form value before a runtime context exists. typescript/ui/field.example:
<Field.Root required invalid={name().length === 0} validationMessage="Enter a name">
  <Field.Label><Text>Name</Text></Field.Label>
  <Field.Control value={name()} onInput={(event) => setName(event.value ?? "")} />
  <Field.Description><Text>Shown on your profile.</Text></Field.Description>
  <Field.Error><Text>Enter a name.</Text></Field.Error>
</Field.Root>

entries.description: Declare when the controlled validity is expected to be recomputed, Base UI's `validationMode`.

entries.name: validation_debounce
entries.type: pub fn validation_debounce(mut self, debounce: Duration) -> Self
entries.description: Wait this long after a change before revalidating, Base UI's `validationDebounceTime`. The interval is an exact one-shot deadline the application schedules with [`crate::AsyncViewContext::sleep`]; QuickGUI never polls, and a field that is not being typed into owns nothing. It applies to [`FieldValidationTrigger::Change`] only — a blur or a submit is a deliberate boundary and validates immediately. Clamped to [`MAX_FIELD_VALIDATION_DEBOUNCE`].

entries.description: Configures validation debounce value for this part.

entries.name: should_validate
entries.type: pub const fn should_validate(&self, trigger: FieldValidationTrigger) -> bool
entries.description: Whether the declared mode expects this event to recompute validity. A submit always validates; a blur validates on `OnBlur` and `OnChange`; a change validates only on `OnChange`.

entries.name: validation_delay
entries.type: pub const fn validation_delay(&self, trigger: FieldValidationTrigger) -> Option<Duration>
entries.description: How long to wait before recomputing validity for this event, when it validates at all. Returns `None` when the declared mode ignores the event, and `Some(Duration::ZERO)` when it validates immediately, so a listener can branch once instead of re-deriving the policy.

sections.name: Field::root_part
sections.signature: pub fn root_part(&self, root: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate an application-owned structural root without adding role or appearance.

sections.name: Field::label_part
sections.signature: pub fn label_part(&self, label: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate a visible label and give it native label-to-control activation. Use [`Self::passive_label_part`] for button-like controls whose label should name but not activate them.

sections.name: Field::passive_label_part
sections.signature: pub fn passive_label_part(&self, label: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate a label relationship without forwarding pointer activation to the control.

sections.name: Field::control_part
sections.signature: pub fn control_part(&self, control: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the application-owned control with field state and mounted relationships.

sections.name: Field::item_part
sections.signature: pub fn item_part(&self, item: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the caller-owned wrapper around one label/control/description row. Base UI's Field.Item groups the parts of a single field inside a larger fieldset so the row can be styled and laid out as one unit. QuickGUI supplies the stable identity and propagates the field's disabled state; layout and appearance stay application-owned.

sections.name: Field::validity_part
sections.signature: pub fn validity_part(&self, visible: bool, validity: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate a caller-owned part that is shown only for a chosen validity, Base UI's Field.Validity. `visible` is the application's own predicate over [`Self::state`] — "invalid and touched", "valid and dirty", whatever the product means. QuickGUI removes the part from layout, paint, input, and the accessibility tree when the predicate is false, exactly as [`Self::error_part`] does, so an unmatched validity costs nothing.

sections.name: Field::description_part
sections.signature: pub fn description_part(&self, description: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate visible supplementary help for the control.

<Calendar.Root value={date()} onValueChange={setDate} onMonthChange={setMonth}>
  <For each={weeks()}>{(week, weekIndex) =>

    </Calendar.Week>
  }</For>
</Calendar.Root>

entries.name: auto_submit
entries.type: pub fn auto_submit(mut self, form: impl Into<ElementId>) -> Self
entries.description: Submit the named form as soon as the final slot is filled. QuickGUI routes the request through [`crate::EventContext::submit_form`], so the form is validated exactly as a Return press or a submit button would validate it. Pass the id of the nearest mounted [`crate::form`] ancestor.

entries.type: pub fn slot_part_with<V: 'static, Change, Complete>( self, cx: &mut ViewContext<'_, V>, state: &OtpFieldState, index: usize, input: Element, access: StateAccessor<V, OtpFieldState>, on_value_change: Change, on_complete: Complete, ) -> Element where Change: Fn(&mut V, &str, &mut EventContext) + Clone + 'static, Complete: Fn(&mut V, &str, &mut EventContext) + Clone + 'static,
entries.description: Decorate one slot and attach its behavior against a per-instance state accessor.

sections.name: OtpField::root_part
sections.signature: pub fn root_part(self, state: &OtpFieldState, root: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate an application-owned root without adding layout or appearance. The root is the group that names the whole code and carries its validity, so assistive technology announces one field rather than a row of unrelated one-character inputs.

sections.name: OtpField::input_part
sections.signature: pub fn input_part(self, state: &OtpFieldState, index: usize, input: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate one application-owned slot input without adding appearance. Pass a [`crate::text_input`] built from [`OtpFieldState::slot_text`]. QuickGUI adds the stable identity, the slot's position in the code, the masked presentation, and the required and disabled policy. Use [`Self::slot_part`] to attach the behavior as well.

sections.name: OtpField::separator_part
sections.signature: pub fn separator_part(self, index: usize, separator: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate an application-owned separator between two slots. The separator is decorative: it carries a stable identity and the Separator role, and is hidden from assistive technology so it never interrupts the announced code.

sections.name: OtpField::slot_part
sections.signature: pub fn slot_part<V: 'static, Change, Complete>( self, cx: &mut ViewContext<'_, V>, state: &OtpFieldState, index: usize, input: Element, access: fn(&mut V) -> &mut OtpFieldState, on_value_change: Change, on_complete: Complete, ) -> Element where Change: Fn(&mut V, &str, &mut EventContext) + Clone + 'static, Complete: Fn(&mut V, &str, &mut EventContext) + Clone + 'static,
sections.description: Decorate one slot and attach its complete behavior. This registers the slot's input listener and its typed keyboard actions. Install [`otp_field_key_bindings`] once on the application keymap. `on_value_change` runs for every change with the whole code; `on_complete` runs only on the transition into a full code, and is followed by [`Self::auto_submit`] when one is declared.

sections.name: Collapsible::panel_part
sections.signature: pub fn panel_part(self, panel: Element) -> Option<Element>
sections.description: Decorate the panel when it should be mounted. The default closed state returns `None`. Pass the result to [`Element::children`] so the `Option<Element>` composes directly. With [`Self::keep_mounted`], a closed panel remains in the retained tree as `display: none` and therefore contributes no layout, paint, input, or accessibility node.

entries.type: pub const fn keep_mounted(mut self, keep_mounted: bool) -> Self
entries.description: Keep a scrollbar mounted while its axis does not overflow. The default unmounts it, matching Base UI's `keepMounted={false}`. A kept scrollbar is hidden from assistive technology while its axis cannot scroll, so a mounted-but-useless scrollbar is never announced.

sections.name: ScrollArea::root_part
sections.signature: pub fn root_part(self, root: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate an application-owned root without adding layout or appearance.

sections.name: ScrollArea::viewport_part
sections.signature: pub fn viewport_part(self, viewport: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the application-owned scroll container. The viewport clips its content on both axes and carries the ScrollView role. The caller places the content by translating [`Self::content_part`] with the retained offset, which keeps scrolling paint-only and keeps QuickGUI's built-in overlay scrollbar out of a component whose scrollbars the application draws itself.

sections.name: ScrollArea::content_part
sections.signature: pub fn content_part(self, content: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the application-owned scrolled content. Translate it by the negated [`ScrollAreaState::offset`]; QuickGUI adds no transform of its own so the application keeps full control of the motion.

sections.name: ScrollArea::scrollbar_part
sections.signature: pub fn scrollbar_part( self, state: &ScrollAreaState, orientation: ScrollAreaOrientation, scrollbar: Element, ) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate one application-owned scrollbar track. The track projects the ScrollBar role with the exact current position, the scrollable range, and its orientation. It is not focusable: a scrollbar duplicates keyboard scrolling the viewport already provides, so it stays out of the Tab sequence.

sections.name: ScrollArea::thumb_part
sections.signature: pub fn thumb_part(self, orientation: ScrollAreaOrientation, thumb: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate one application-owned scrollbar thumb. The thumb carries the captured pointer drag. Attach a [`crate::ViewContext::pointer_listener`] registered for [`Self::thumb_id`] and forward the event to [`ScrollAreaState::apply_thumb_pointer`] with the track length the caller laid out.

sections.name: ScrollArea::positioned_thumb_part
sections.signature: pub fn positioned_thumb_part( self, state: &ScrollAreaState, orientation: ScrollAreaOrientation, track_length: f32, thumb: Element, ) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate and position one application-owned scrollbar thumb inside its scrollbar. This is [`Self::thumb_part`] plus the structural geometry a draggable thumb needs: the thumb is absolutely positioned along the scrollbar's axis at [`ScrollAreaState::thumb_offset`] with [`ScrollAreaState::thumb_length`], so it follows the offset without the application re-deriving either value. Cross-axis size and every visual property stay application-owned.

sections.name: ScrollArea::corner_part
sections.signature: pub fn corner_part(self, corner: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the application-owned corner between a horizontal and a vertical scrollbar.

<Table.Root
  columns={[{ id: "name", label: "Name" }, { id: "status", label: "Status" }]}
  rowCount={rows.length}
  onVisibleRangeChange={setVisibleRange}
>
  <Table.Header column="name"><Text>Name</Text></Table.Header>
  <For each={visibleRows()}>{(row) =>
    <Table.Row index={row.index}>
      <Table.Cell column="name"><Text>{row.name}</Text></Table.Cell>
      <Table.Cell column="status"><Text>{row.status}</Text></Table.Cell>
    </Table.Row>
  }</For>
</Table.Root>

entries.type: pub fn element<V, H, E, RenderHeader, RenderCell, Activate>( &mut self, cx: &mut ViewContext<'_, V>, id: impl Into<ElementId>, columns: &[TableColumn], access: fn(&mut V) -> &mut TableState, render_header: RenderHeader, render_cell: RenderCell, activate: Activate, ) -> Element where V: 'static, H: IntoElement, E: IntoElement, RenderHeader: FnMut(TableHeaderState<'_>) -> H, RenderCell: FnMut(TableCellState<'_>) -> E, Activate: Fn(&mut V, TableCellPosition, &mut EventContext) + Clone + 'static,
entries.description: Build a complete unstyled virtualized, sortable, keyboard-navigable table. `render_header` owns every visible header declaration, including label, sort indicator, and the placement of the resize handle QuickGUI hands it. `render_cell` owns every visible cell declaration, including the inline editor it mounts while `editing` is set, and runs only for mounted rows. QuickGUI decorates those elements with fixed grid geometry, identities, pointer/keyboard behavior, and accessibility semantics but adds no paint. `activate` receives the current logical cell when Return is dispatched outside an editor; selection, sort, width, order, and editing state remain directly readable from `access`.

entries.name: element_with
entries.type: pub fn element_with<V, H, E, RenderHeader, RenderCell, Activate>( &mut self, cx: &mut ViewContext<'_, V>, id: impl Into<ElementId>, columns: &[TableColumn], access_source: StateAccessor<V, TableState>, render_header: RenderHeader, render_cell: RenderCell, activate: Activate, ) -> Element where V: 'static, H: IntoElement, E: IntoElement, RenderHeader: FnMut(TableHeaderState<'_>) -> H, RenderCell: FnMut(TableCellState<'_>) -> E, Activate: Fn(&mut V, TableCellPosition, &mut EventContext) + Clone + 'static,
entries.description: Build the table against a per-instance retained-state accessor. A host that renders many declared tables through one view passes an accessor that captures which [`TableState`] each registered listener resolves. Every row is a plain container; [`Self::element_with_rows`] lets the caller paint the rows too.

entries.name: element_with_rows
entries.type: pub fn element_with_rows<V, R, H, E, RenderRow, RenderHeader, RenderCell, Activate>( &mut self, cx: &mut ViewContext<'_, V>, id: impl Into<ElementId>, columns: &[TableColumn], access_source: StateAccessor<V, TableState>, mut render_row: RenderRow, mut render_header: RenderHeader, mut render_cell: RenderCell, activate: Activate, ) -> Element where V: 'static, R: IntoElement, H: IntoElement, E: IntoElement, RenderRow: FnMut(TableRowState) -> R, RenderHeader: FnMut(TableHeaderState<'_>) -> H, RenderCell: FnMut(TableCellState<'_>) -> E, Activate: Fn(&mut V, TableCellPosition, &mut EventContext) + Clone + 'static,
entries.description: Build the table with a caller-owned container for every mounted row. `render_row` returns the element a row's cells are laid out in. QuickGUI adds the grid tracks, the row height, the row identity, and the collection semantics on top of it, so the caller declares only the row's paint — a background, a divider, a hover state, or a [`selected_style`](Element::selected_style) that paints while the row is selected — never its layout. The renderer runs only for mounted rows.

entries.description: Supply the children of a pending branch in one atomic, validated splice. The replacement is built and validated before any live state changes: an over-deep, oversize, or duplicate-ID payload leaves the tree exactly as it was. On success the branch stops being pending, its placeholder row disappears, and selection, expansion, and the logical scroll anchor are preserved. An unknown node ID reports `Ok(false)`.

entries.name: element
entries.type: pub fn element<V, E, RenderRow, Activate>( &mut self, cx: &mut ViewContext<'_, V>, id: impl Into<ElementId>, access: fn(&mut V) -> &mut TreeState<T>, render_row: RenderRow, activate: Activate, ) -> Element where V: 'static, T: 'static, E: IntoElement, RenderRow: FnMut(TreeRow<'_, T>, Option<Element>) -> E, Activate: Fn(&mut V, ElementId, &mut EventContext) + Clone + 'static,
entries.description: Build a complete unstyled virtualized, expandable, keyboard-navigable tree. `render_row` runs only for mounted rows and receives an optional behavior-decorated, appearance-free disclosure element. The caller decides where to place that control and owns the complete row layout and paint. QuickGUI decorates the returned row with fixed virtual geometry, tree semantics, selection, and pointer behavior. `activate` receives the selected application value by stable node ID; the tree retains no closure or scheduler afterward.

sections.name: Avatar
sections.signature: pub fn new(root_id: impl Into<ElementId>, label: impl Into<Arc<str>>) -> Self
sections.description: Declare an avatar with the accessible name assistive technology announces.

entries.name: root_id
entries.description: Configures root id for this part.

entries.name: label
entries.description: Configures label for this part.

entries.name: image_id
entries.description: Configures image id for this part.

entries.name: fallback_id
entries.description: Configures fallback id for this part.

entries.name: apply_loading_status
entries.type: pub fn apply_loading_status<V: 'static>( view: &mut V, cx: &mut EventContext, access: &StateAccessor<V, AvatarState>, status: AvatarLoadingStatus, now: Instant, on_loading_status_change: impl FnOnce(&mut V, AvatarLoadingStatus, &mut EventContext), ) -> bool
entries.description: Apply a load status reported by the application and notify the owner exactly once. QuickGUI decodes images on a worker pool without a per-element completion event, so the application reports the status it already knows — from its own `cx.spawn` load, an [`crate::ImageResource`] loader, or a hosted renderer — and this is the `onLoadingStatusChange` counterpart: the retained status changes, the exact fallback deadline is re-armed, and `on_loading_status_change` runs only for a real transition. Returns whether the retained state changed.

entries.name: schedule
entries.type: pub fn schedule<V: 'static>(cx: &mut ViewContext<'_, V>, state: &AvatarState)
entries.description: Ask for the one repaint an armed fallback deadline needs. Call this while rendering. A settled avatar requests nothing, so the window stays asleep.

sections.name: Avatar::root_part
sections.signature: pub fn root_part(&self, root: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate an application-owned root without adding layout or appearance. The root carries the whole avatar's Image role and accessible name, so swapping between the image and the fallback never changes what is announced.

sections.name: Avatar::image_part
sections.signature: pub fn image_part(&self, image: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the application-owned image without adding appearance. Pass a [`crate::img`] built from the caller's own source. Mount it only while [`AvatarState::shows_image`] is true; the part is hidden from assistive technology because the root already names the avatar.

sections.name: Avatar::fallback_part
sections.signature: pub fn fallback_part(&self, fallback: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the application-owned fallback without adding appearance. Mount it only while [`AvatarState::shows_fallback`] is true.

sections.name: avatar
sections.signature: pub fn avatar(id: impl Into<ElementId>, label: impl Into<Arc<str>>) -> Element
sections.description: Create an unstyled avatar root. This shorthand is equivalent to `Avatar::new(id, label).root_part(div())`.

sections.name: Progress
sections.signature: pub fn new(value: f64, maximum: f64) -> Self
sections.description: Create a determinate indicator between `0.0` and `maximum`. A non-finite or non-positive maximum falls back to `1.0`; the value is clamped into range.

entries.name: fraction
entries.description: Create a determinate indicator from a `0.0..=1.0` completion fraction.

entries.name: indeterminate
entries.description: Create an indicator for work whose completion is unknown.

entries.name: value_text
entries.type: pub fn value_text(mut self, text: impl Into<Arc<str>>) -> Self
entries.description: Attach a human-readable value such as `"3 of 12 files"`. Assistive technology prefers this over the raw number when present. An empty string clears it. The text is not rendered; the application owns every visible label.

entries.name: id
entries.type: pub fn id(mut self, id: impl Into<ElementId>) -> Self
entries.description: Give this indicator a stable identity so its label and value parts can be related to it. Without an identity the parts are still decorated, but QuickGUI cannot point the root's accessible name and description at them, so the application supplies its own `accessibility_label`. Existing code that never declares an identity is unchanged.

entries.name: format
entries.type: pub fn format(mut self, format: ValueFormat) -> Self
entries.description: Attach a bounded value formatter, Base UI's `format` prop. The result is what [`Self::display_value`] returns for a caller-owned value part, and what assistive technology reads unless [`Self::value_text`] overrides it.

entries.name: status
entries.description: Which of Base UI's three progress states this indicator is in.

entries.name: state
entries.description: A copyable snapshot of what Base UI exposes as `data-*` attributes.

entries.name: display_value
entries.description: The formatted text for a caller-owned value part, or `None` while indeterminate.

entries.name: accessible_value
entries.description: The text assistive technology reads for the value, if any. An explicit [`Self::value_text`] wins over [`Self::format`], matching Base UI's `getAriaValueText` precedence.

entries.name: label_id
entries.description: Stable identity of the label part, when this indicator declares one.

entries.name: value_id
entries.description: Stable identity of the value part, when this indicator declares one.

entries.name: track_id
entries.description: Stable identity of the track part, when this indicator declares one.

entries.name: indicator_id
entries.description: Stable identity of the indicator part, when this indicator declares one.

entries.name: value
entries.description: Configures value for this part.

entries.name: maximum
entries.description: Configures maximum for this part.

entries.name: is_indeterminate
entries.description: Configures is indeterminate for this part.

entries.name: completion
entries.description: The `0.0..=1.0` completion fraction, or `None` while indeterminate. Applications use this to size a caller-owned fill.

sections.name: Progress::root_part
sections.signature: pub fn root_part(&self, root: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate an application-owned root without adding layout or appearance.

sections.name: Progress::track_part
sections.signature: pub fn track_part(&self, track: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the caller-owned track that the fill is measured inside. The track is decoration: the root already carries the numeric value and bounds, so the track and everything under it stay out of the accessible name.

sections.name: Progress::indicator_part
sections.signature: pub fn indicator_part(&self, indicator: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Hide an application-owned fill or animation from the accessible name.

sections.name: Progress::label_part
sections.signature: pub fn label_part(&self, label: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Assign the stable mounted label target the root points at.

sections.name: Progress::value_part
sections.signature: pub fn value_part(&self, value: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Assign the stable mounted value target the root points at. Put [`Self::display_value`] inside it; QuickGUI never renders the text itself.

sections.name: progress
sections.signature: pub fn progress(value: f64, maximum: f64) -> Element
sections.description: Create an unstyled determinate progress root. This shorthand is equivalent to `Progress::new(value, maximum).root_part(div())`.

sections.name: Meter
sections.signature: pub fn new(value: f64, minimum: f64, maximum: f64) -> Self
sections.description: Create a meter. Non-finite bounds fall back to `0.0..=1.0` and an inverted range is swapped.

entries.name: low
entries.type: pub fn low(mut self, low: f64) -> Self
entries.description: Mark the upper end of the low range. Values outside the meter bounds are clamped.

entries.name: high
entries.type: pub fn high(mut self, high: f64) -> Self
entries.description: Mark the lower end of the high range.

entries.name: optimum
entries.type: pub fn optimum(mut self, optimum: f64) -> Self
entries.description: Mark the most favorable value inside the range.

entries.name: id
entries.type: pub fn id(mut self, id: impl Into<ElementId>) -> Self
entries.description: Give this meter a stable identity so its label and value parts can be related to it.

entries.name: format
entries.type: pub fn format(mut self, format: ValueFormat) -> Self
entries.description: Attach a bounded value formatter, Base UI's `format` prop.

entries.name: value_text
entries.type: pub fn value_text(mut self, text: impl Into<Arc<str>>) -> Self
entries.description: Attach a human-readable value that assistive technology prefers over the raw number. This is Base UI's `getAriaValueText`; an empty string clears it. It wins over [`Self::format`].

entries.name: display_value
entries.description: The formatted text for a caller-owned value part.

entries.name: accessible_value
entries.description: The text assistive technology reads for the value, if any.

entries.name: label_id
entries.description: Stable identity of the label part, when this meter declares one.

entries.name: value_id
entries.description: Stable identity of the value part, when this meter declares one.

entries.name: track_id
entries.description: Stable identity of the track part, when this meter declares one.

entries.name: indicator_id
entries.description: Stable identity of the indicator part, when this meter declares one.

entries.name: value
entries.description: Configures value for this part.

entries.name: minimum
entries.description: Configures minimum for this part.

entries.name: maximum
entries.description: Configures maximum for this part.

entries.name: low_value
entries.description: Configures low value for this part.

entries.name: high_value
entries.description: Configures high value for this part.

entries.name: optimum_value
entries.description: Configures optimum value for this part.

entries.name: completion
entries.description: The `0.0..=1.0` position of the value inside the meter's range.

entries.name: is_low
entries.description: Whether the value falls at or below [`Self::low`].

entries.name: is_high
entries.description: Whether the value falls at or above [`Self::high`].

sections.name: Meter::root_part
sections.signature: pub fn root_part(&self, root: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate an application-owned root without adding layout or appearance.

sections.name: Meter::track_part
sections.signature: pub fn track_part(&self, track: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the caller-owned track that the fill is measured inside.

sections.name: Meter::indicator_part
sections.signature: pub fn indicator_part(&self, indicator: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Hide an application-owned fill from the accessible name.

sections.name: Meter::label_part
sections.signature: pub fn label_part(&self, label: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Assign the stable mounted label target the root points at.

sections.name: Meter::value_part
sections.signature: pub fn value_part(&self, value: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Assign the stable mounted value target the root points at.

sections.name: meter
sections.signature: pub fn meter(value: f64, minimum: f64, maximum: f64) -> Element
sections.description: Create an unstyled meter root. This shorthand is equivalent to `Meter::new(value, minimum, maximum).root_part(div())`.

entries.name: Ref
entries.description: Receives the retained native node after construction. Keep imperative work in event or lifecycle callbacks.

entries.name: Style
entries.description: Reusable layout, typography, color, and interaction-state styles. Build with ui.Style() and compose with Merge.

entries.name: Children
entries.description: Content mounted inside the component. Compound child callbacks run after the parent context exists.

entries.name: Disabled
entries.description: Prevents activation and exposes the disabled state to accessibility. Compound parts inherit a disabled root.

entries.name: Role

sections.name: Toolbar::root_part
sections.signature: pub fn root_part(self, root: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate an application-owned toolbar root without adding layout or appearance.

sections.name: Toolbar::group_part
sections.signature: pub fn group_part(self, group: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate a caller-owned group of related toolbar items, Base UI's Toolbar.Group. The group is a labelling and structural unit only: every item inside it keeps taking part in the toolbar's single roving Tab stop, so grouping never creates a second focus scope.

sections.name: Toolbar::separator_part
sections.signature: pub fn separator_part(self, separator: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate a caller-owned divider between toolbar groups, Base UI's Toolbar.Separator. A separator carries the Separator role across the toolbar's cross axis and never takes focus, so arrow navigation steps straight past it.

sections.name: Popover
sections.signature: pub fn new( trigger_id: impl Into<ElementId>, surface_id: impl Into<ElementId>, open: bool, ) -> Self

entries.name: open
entries.type: pub const fn open(mut self, open: bool) -> Self
entries.description: Replace the controlled open flag, Base UI's Root `open` prop. The descriptor is copied per frame, so a component that retains the open flag itself can build one descriptor at construction time and stamp the current value onto it here.

entries.name: kind
entries.type: pub const fn kind(mut self, kind: PopoverKind) -> Self
entries.description: Configures kind for this part.

entries.name: placement
entries.type: pub const fn placement(mut self, placement: AnchorPlacement) -> Self
entries.description: Configures placement for this part.

entries.name: side
entries.type: pub const fn side(self, side: AnchorSide) -> Self
entries.description: Prefer one side of the anchor, keeping the current cross-axis alignment. This is the side half of [`Self::placement`], matching Base UI's `side` prop. A side is a preference: QuickGUI flips to the opposite side when the preferred one does not fit, and [`Self::resolved_side`] reports what actually happened.

entries.name: align
entries.type: pub const fn align(self, align: AnchorAlign) -> Self
entries.description: Prefer a cross-axis alignment, keeping the current side. This is the alignment half of [`Self::placement`], matching Base UI's `align` prop.

entries.name: side_offset
entries.type: pub fn side_offset(self, offset: f32) -> Self
entries.description: Set the distance between the anchor and the positioner, Base UI's `sideOffset`. This is the Base UI-named alias of [`Self::anchor_gap`]. Both names stay supported and write the same bounded value.

entries.name: align_offset
entries.type: pub fn align_offset(mut self, offset: f32) -> Self
entries.description: Shift the popover along its cross axis before collision handling, Base UI's `alignOffset`. Positive values move right on a top or bottom placement and down on a left or right placement. The shift runs before the surface is clamped into the viewport, so it can slide a popup along its trigger but never push it off screen.

entries.name: collision_padding
entries.type: pub fn collision_padding(self, padding: f32) -> Self
entries.description: Set the collision padding kept inside the window viewport, Base UI's `collisionPadding`. This is the Base UI-named alias of [`Self::viewport_margin`]. Both names stay supported.

entries.name: sticky
entries.type: pub const fn sticky(mut self, sticky: bool) -> Self
entries.description: Choose whether the popover is kept inside the collision viewport, Base UI's `sticky`. QuickGUI keeps anchored surfaces on screen by default, which is Base UI's sticky behavior. Passing `false` locks the popover to its anchor so it travels off screen with a scrolling row instead of detaching from it.

entries.name: anchor_element
entries.type: pub fn anchor_element(mut self, anchor: impl Into<ElementId>) -> Self
entries.description: Position against a different mounted element instead of the trigger, Base UI's `anchor`.

entries.name: anchor_point
entries.type: pub fn anchor_point(mut self, anchor: Point) -> Self
entries.description: Position against a logical window point instead of the trigger, Base UI's virtual `anchor`.

entries.name: anchor_trigger
entries.type: pub const fn anchor_trigger(mut self) -> Self
entries.description: Position against the trigger again, undoing an anchor override.

entries.name: modal
entries.type: pub const fn modal(mut self, modal: bool) -> Self
entries.description: Make the open popover modal, Base UI's `modal` prop. A modal popover contains Tab focus inside the popup and expects a mounted [`Self::backdrop_part`] to absorb outside pointer input. QuickGUI adds no dimming: the backdrop stays an invisible caller-owned element until the application paints it.

entries.name: is_modal
entries.description: Whether this popover contains focus while open.

entries.name: arrow_size
entries.type: pub fn arrow_size(mut self, size: f32) -> Self
entries.description: Declare the edge length of a framework-positioned arrow. [`Self::arrow_part`] centers an arrow of this size on the anchor. Leaving it at zero pins the arrow to the resolved edge without a cross-axis offset, which is what an application that centers the arrow with its own layout wants.

entries.name: arrow_padding
entries.type: pub fn arrow_padding(mut self, padding: f32) -> Self
entries.description: Keep a framework-positioned arrow this far from the popup's corners, Base UI's `arrowPadding`.

entries.name: track_placement
entries.type: pub fn track_placement(mut self, placement: &AnchorPlacementHandle) -> Self
entries.description: Adopt the placement QuickGUI resolved for this popover on the previous painted frame. Store an [`AnchorPlacementHandle`] on the view next to `open`, mount the positioner with [`Self::tracked_positioner_part`] or [`Self::tracked_surface_part`], and pass the handle here while declaring the next frame. [`Self::arrow_part`], [`Self::resolved_side`], [`Self::resolved_align`], and [`Self::state`] then follow the placement the popover really used instead of the declared preference. QuickGUI requests exactly one correcting frame when the resolved placement changes, so a flipped popover settles immediately and an unflipped one adds no redraw source.

entries.name: resolved_placement
entries.type: pub const fn resolved_placement(mut self, resolved: Option<ResolvedAnchorPlacement>) -> Self
entries.description: Adopt an already-read placement report. Use this when the application keeps the snapshot itself rather than the handle.

entries.name: resolved_side
entries.description: The side the popover actually opened on, or the declared preference before the first frame.

entries.name: resolved_align
entries.description: The cross-axis alignment the popover actually used, or the declared preference.

entries.name: resolved_anchor_placement
entries.description: The full placement the popover actually used, or the declared preference.

entries.name: state
entries.description: A copyable snapshot of what Base UI exposes as `data-*` attributes and CSS variables. The application styles from this: it picks a transform origin from [`PopoverPartState::side`], hides a popup whose anchor scrolled away using [`PopoverPartState::anchor_hidden`], matches the trigger width with [`PopoverPartState::anchor_width`], and caps a scrolling viewport with [`PopoverPartState::available_height`]. Every measured field stays zero until the popover has been painted once with a bound placement handle.

entries.name: anchor_gap

entries.description: Set the structural distance between the trigger and positioner.

entries.description: Set the structural collision margin inside the current window viewport.

sections.name: Popover::trigger_part
sections.signature: pub fn trigger_part(self, trigger: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate an application-owned trigger without adding appearance.

sections.name: Popover::positioner_part
sections.signature: pub fn positioner_part(self, positioner: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the caller-owned portal/positioner without adding popover appearance. QuickGUI's retained overlay node is itself the portal, so this part combines the Base UI-style Portal and Positioner boundary without introducing a full-window wrapper that would block unrelated pointer input.

sections.name: Popover::tracked_positioner_part
sections.signature: pub fn tracked_positioner_part( self, positioner: Element, placement: &AnchorPlacementHandle, ) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the positioner and publish the placement it resolves to. This is [`Self::positioner_part`] plus [`crate::Element::report_anchor_placement`]: the handle receives the side, alignment, anchor rectangle, and remaining room the popover actually used, and [`Self::track_placement`] feeds it back into the descriptor on the next frame.

sections.name: Popover::portal_part
sections.signature: pub fn portal_part(self, portal: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Base UI's Portal name for the combined portal/positioner part. QuickGUI's retained overlay node is itself the portal, so Portal and Positioner are one element; both names decorate it identically.

sections.name: Popover::popover_part
sections.signature: pub fn popover_part(self, popover: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate an application-owned popover without adding layout or appearance. The popover emits [`crate::Event::Dismiss`] under [`Self::surface_id`] for every enabled dismissal path. Mounted title/description parts are related without copying their text.

sections.name: Popover::surface_part
sections.signature: pub fn surface_part(self, surface: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate one caller-owned element as both positioner and popover. This compact form has the same unstyled contract as composing [`Self::positioner_part`] around [`Self::popover_part`]. Use separate parts when the application needs to animate or size the positioner independently from popover presentation.

sections.name: Popover::tracked_surface_part
sections.signature: pub fn tracked_surface_part( self, surface: Element, placement: &AnchorPlacementHandle, ) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the merged surface and publish the placement it resolves to.

sections.name: Popover::arrow_part
sections.signature: pub fn arrow_part(self, arrow: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Position a caller-owned arrow on the edge the popover actually opened against. The arrow is absolutely positioned inside the popup, pinned to the edge that faces the anchor and centered on the anchor along the cross axis. When [`Self::track_placement`] has supplied a placement report the offsets follow the real placement, including a flip — never the declared preference. Before the first painted frame, or without a bound handle, the arrow follows the declared side and stays centered on the popup, and QuickGUI's one correcting frame moves it as soon as the real placement is known. The application owns the arrow's size, shape, rotation, and color. Declare [`Self::arrow_size`] when QuickGUI should center an arrow of a known edge length, and [`Self::arrow_padding`] to keep it clear of the popup's corners. The arrow is hidden from assistive technology: it is decoration attached to a surface that already carries the relationship.

sections.name: Popover::viewport_part
sections.signature: pub fn viewport_part(self, viewport: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate a caller-owned scrolling viewport mounted inside the popup. Base UI's Viewport clips content that changes size between triggers so the popup can animate between them. QuickGUI supplies the stable identity and the scroll container; height, padding, and motion stay application-owned — cap it with [`PopoverPartState::available_height`] to keep a long popup inside the window.

sections.name: Popover::backdrop_part
sections.signature: pub fn backdrop_part(self, backdrop: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate an optional caller-painted viewport backdrop.

sections.name: Popover::title_part
sections.signature: pub fn title_part(self, title: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Assign the stable mounted label target used by the popover.

sections.name: Popover::description_part
sections.signature: pub fn description_part(self, description: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Assign the stable mounted description target used by the popover.

sections.name: Popover::close_part
sections.signature: pub fn close_part(self, label: impl Into<Arc<str>>, close: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate a caller-owned close control with button behavior and no visual defaults.

typescript/ui/dialog.example:
<Dialog.Root open={open()} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
  <Dialog.Trigger><Text>Edit profile</Text></Dialog.Trigger>
  <Dialog.Portal>
    <Dialog.Backdrop />
    <Dialog.Viewport>
      <Dialog.Popup>
        <Dialog.Title><Text>Edit profile</Text></Dialog.Title>
        <Dialog.Description><Text>Changes are saved immediately.</Text></Dialog.Description>
        <Dialog.Close><Text>Done</Text></Dialog.Close>
      </Dialog.Popup>
    </Dialog.Viewport>
  </Dialog.Portal>
</Dialog.Root>

sections.description: Decorate an application-owned trigger without adding appearance.

sections.description: Decorate the full-window portal and active modal focus boundary.

sections.name: Dialog::backdrop_part
sections.signature: pub fn backdrop_part(self, backdrop: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the caller-owned visual backdrop.

sections.name: Dialog::popover_part
sections.signature: pub fn popover_part(self, popover: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the caller-owned modal popover. The popover is a negative-Tab-index focus fallback. Enabled descendant Tab stops are chosen first when the enclosing trap mounts. Title and description relationships project only when the corresponding parts are mounted, so incomplete compositions never emit dangling native node references.

sections.name: Dialog::viewport_part
sections.signature: pub fn viewport_part(self, viewport: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the caller-owned scrolling viewport the popup sits inside, Base UI's Viewport. A dialog taller than the window must scroll as one surface rather than clipping its own content, and the scroll must live outside the popup so the popup keeps its own padding and shadow. QuickGUI supplies the stable identity and the scroll container; size, alignment, and padding stay application-owned.

sections.description: Assign the stable visible label target used by the popover.

sections.description: Assign the stable visible description target used by the popover.

sections.description: Decorate a caller-owned close control with button behavior and no visual defaults.

typescript/ui/alert-dialog.example:
<AlertDialog.Root open={open()} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
  <AlertDialog.Trigger><Text>Delete project</Text></AlertDialog.Trigger>
  <AlertDialog.Portal>
    <AlertDialog.Backdrop />
    <AlertDialog.Viewport>
      <AlertDialog.Popup>
        <AlertDialog.Title><Text>Delete this project?</Text></AlertDialog.Title>
        <AlertDialog.Description><Text>This cannot be undone.</Text></AlertDialog.Description>
        <AlertDialog.Close><Text>Cancel</Text></AlertDialog.Close>
      </AlertDialog.Popup>
    </AlertDialog.Viewport>
  </AlertDialog.Portal>
</AlertDialog.Root>

sections.name: Dialog::trigger_part
sections.signature: pub fn trigger_part(self, id: impl Into<ElementId>, trigger: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate an application-owned trigger without adding appearance.

sections.name: Dialog::root_part
sections.signature: pub fn root_part(self, root: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the full-window portal and active modal focus boundary.

sections.name: Dialog::backdrop_part
sections.signature: pub fn backdrop_part(self, backdrop: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the caller-owned visual backdrop.

sections.name: Dialog::popover_part
sections.signature: pub fn popover_part(self, popover: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the caller-owned modal popover. The popover is a negative-Tab-index focus fallback. Enabled descendant Tab stops are chosen first when the enclosing trap mounts. Title and description relationships project only when the corresponding parts are mounted, so incomplete compositions never emit dangling native node references.

sections.name: Dialog::viewport_part
sections.signature: pub fn viewport_part(self, viewport: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the caller-owned scrolling viewport the popup sits inside, Base UI's Viewport. A dialog taller than the window must scroll as one surface rather than clipping its own content, and the scroll must live outside the popup so the popup keeps its own padding and shadow. QuickGUI supplies the stable identity and the scroll container; size, alignment, and padding stay application-owned.

sections.name: Dialog::title_part
sections.signature: pub fn title_part(self, title: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Assign the stable visible label target used by the popover.

sections.name: Dialog::description_part
sections.signature: pub fn description_part(self, description: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Assign the stable visible description target used by the popover.

sections.name: Dialog::close_part
sections.signature: pub fn close_part(self, label: impl Into<std::sync::Arc<str>>, close: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate a caller-owned close control with button behavior and no visual defaults.

sections.name: PreviewCard
sections.signature: pub fn new( trigger_id: impl Into<ElementId>, popup_id: impl Into<ElementId>, open: bool, ) -> Self
sections.description: Declare a preview card over caller-owned trigger and popup identities.

entries.name: from_state
entries.type: pub fn from_state( trigger_id: impl Into<ElementId>, popup_id: impl Into<ElementId>, state: &PreviewCardState, ) -> Self
entries.description: Declare a preview card from its retained state.

entries.name: placement
entries.type: pub const fn placement(mut self, placement: AnchorPlacement) -> Self
entries.description: Configures placement for this part.

entries.name: anchor_gap
entries.type: pub fn anchor_gap(mut self, gap: f32) -> Self
entries.description: Set the structural distance between the trigger and the popup.

entries.name: viewport_margin
entries.type: pub fn viewport_margin(mut self, margin: f32) -> Self
entries.description: Set the structural collision margin inside the current window viewport.

entries.name: popover
entries.description: The composed popover, for callers that need its remaining parts directly.

entries.name: is_open
entries.description: Configures is open for this part.

entries.name: trigger_id
entries.description: Configures trigger id for this part.

entries.name: popup_id
entries.description: Configures popup id for this part.

entries.name: positioner_id
entries.description: Configures positioner id for this part.

entries.name: backdrop_id
entries.description: Configures backdrop id for this part.

entries.name: arrow_id
entries.description: Configures arrow id for this part.

entries.name: trigger_focus
entries.description: Configures trigger focus for this part.

entries.name: on_trigger_hover
entries.type: pub fn on_trigger_hover<V: 'static, Change>( self, cx: &mut ViewContext<'_, V>, access: fn(&mut V) -> &mut PreviewCardState, on_open_change: Change, ) -> HoverListener<V> where Change: Fn(&mut V, bool, &mut EventContext) + 'static,
entries.description: Build the trigger's hover behavior. Attach the returned handle with [`crate::Element::on_hover`]. `on_open_change` runs only when the open value actually changes, which for the delayed open is on the frame the deadline is applied rather than on the pointer event that armed it.

entries.name: on_trigger_hover_with
entries.type: pub fn on_trigger_hover_with<V: 'static, Change>( self, cx: &mut ViewContext<'_, V>, access: StateAccessor<V, PreviewCardState>, on_open_change: Change, ) -> HoverListener<V> where Change: Fn(&mut V, bool, &mut EventContext) + 'static,
entries.description: Build the trigger's hover behavior against a per-instance state accessor.

entries.name: on_popup_hover
entries.type: pub fn on_popup_hover<V: 'static, Change>( self, cx: &mut ViewContext<'_, V>, access: fn(&mut V) -> &mut PreviewCardState, on_open_change: Change, ) -> HoverListener<V> where Change: Fn(&mut V, bool, &mut EventContext) + 'static,
entries.description: Build the popup's hover behavior, which keeps an open card open.

entries.name: on_popup_hover_with
entries.type: pub fn on_popup_hover_with<V: 'static, Change>( self, cx: &mut ViewContext<'_, V>, access: StateAccessor<V, PreviewCardState>, on_open_change: Change, ) -> HoverListener<V> where Change: Fn(&mut V, bool, &mut EventContext) + 'static,
entries.description: Build the popup's hover behavior against a per-instance state accessor.

entries.name: on_dismiss
entries.type: pub fn on_dismiss<V: 'static, Change>( self, cx: &mut ViewContext<'_, V>, access: fn(&mut V) -> &mut PreviewCardState, on_open_change: Change, ) -> DismissListener<V> where Change: Fn(&mut V, bool, &mut EventContext) + 'static,
entries.description: Build the popup's dismissal behavior for Escape and outside presses. Attach the returned handle with [`crate::Element::on_dismiss`].

entries.name: on_dismiss_with
entries.type: pub fn on_dismiss_with<V: 'static, Change>( self, cx: &mut ViewContext<'_, V>, access: StateAccessor<V, PreviewCardState>, on_open_change: Change, ) -> DismissListener<V> where Change: Fn(&mut V, bool, &mut EventContext) + 'static,
entries.description: Build the popup's dismissal behavior against a per-instance state accessor.

entries.name: schedule
entries.type: pub fn schedule<V: 'static>(cx: &mut ViewContext<'_, V>, state: &PreviewCardState)
entries.description: Ask for the one repaint an armed open or close deadline needs. Call this while rendering. A settled preview card requests nothing, so the window sleeps.

sections.name: PreviewCard::root_part
sections.signature: pub fn root_part(self, root: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the optional application-owned structural wrapper. A preview card needs no wrapper of its own; this part exists so a composition that wants one keeps the trigger out of the window's native drag region without inventing appearance.

sections.name: PreviewCard::trigger_part
sections.signature: pub fn trigger_part(self, trigger: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the application-owned link-like trigger without adding appearance. Unlike a popover trigger, this projects the Link role: a preview card previews a destination rather than opening a menu, so the trigger stays an ordinary link for the keyboard and for assistive technology.

sections.name: PreviewCard::portal_part
sections.signature: pub fn portal_part(self, portal: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the caller-owned portal boundary. QuickGUI's retained overlay node is itself the portal, so this is the same boundary as [`Self::positioner_part`]; mount exactly one of them.

sections.name: PreviewCard::positioner_part
sections.signature: pub fn positioner_part(self, positioner: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the caller-owned positioner without adding appearance.

sections.name: PreviewCard::popup_part
sections.signature: pub fn popup_part(self, popup: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the application-owned popup without adding layout or appearance. The popup emits [`crate::Event::Dismiss`] under [`Self::popup_id`] for Escape and for an outside pointer press, and restores focus to the trigger.

sections.name: PreviewCard::arrow_part
sections.signature: pub fn arrow_part(self, arrow: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the application-owned arrow. The arrow is decorative: it carries a stable identity so the application can position and animate it, and is hidden from assistive technology.

sections.name: PreviewCard::backdrop_part
sections.signature: pub fn backdrop_part(self, backdrop: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate an optional caller-painted viewport backdrop.

typescript/ui/toast.example:
const toast = useToastManager();

toast.add({ id: "saved", title: "Saved", description: "Your changes are live." });

<Toast.Provider timeout={5000} limit={3}>
  <Toast.Portal>
    <Toast.Viewport toasts={toast.toasts()} onDismiss={toast.dismiss}>
      <For each={toast.toasts()}>{(item) =>
        <Toast.Root toastId={item.id}>
          <Toast.Content><Toast.Title /><Toast.Description /></Toast.Content>
          <Toast.Close><Text>Close</Text></Toast.Close>
        </Toast.Root>
      }</For>
    </Toast.Viewport>
  </Toast.Portal>
</Toast.Provider>

A horizontal menu installs [`POPOVER_MENU_HORIZONTAL_KEY_CONTEXT`] instead of [`POPOVER_MENU_KEY_CONTEXT`], so Left and Right move between top-level triggers and Down opens the highlighted submenu. Nothing else about the model changes.

entries.description: Replace the orientation in place, reporting whether it changed.

entries.name: radio_value

entries.description: The item currently checked in one radio group, Base UI's `Menu.RadioGroup` `value`.

entries.name: set_radio_value
entries.type: pub fn set_radio_value( &mut self, group: impl Into<ElementId>, value: impl Into<ElementId>, ) -> bool
entries.description: Check exactly one item in a radio group, Base UI's `Menu.RadioGroup` `onValueChange`. Every other item in the group is unchecked in the same update, so a group can never retain two checked values. Returns whether anything changed; an item ID that is not a radio item in `group` changes nothing.

entries.name: set_items

entries.description: Atomically replace the menu contents while preserving the highlighted stable ID.

entries.name: unhighlight
entries.type: pub fn unhighlight(&mut self, index: usize) -> bool
entries.description: Drop the highlight from `index` when the pointer leaves it, returning whether it changed. A native menu shows no highlighted row once the pointer has left the surface, so a row the pointer lit up goes dark when it leaves; a highlight the keyboard moved elsewhere in the meantime is left alone.

entries.description: Update bounded typeahead state and highlight the next prefix match. `now` is supplied by the caller so deterministic tests do not depend on wall-clock sleeps. The return value reports whether the highlighted item changed.

A group label has no command identity, so its accessibility-only identity is derived from the menu root and bounded structural index. Separators intentionally remain anonymous.

entries.name: element
entries.type: pub fn element<V, Render, Dismiss>( &self, cx: &mut ViewContext<'_, V>, id: impl Into<ElementId>, access: fn(&mut V) -> &mut PopoverMenu, root: Element, render_item: Render, dismiss: Dismiss, ) -> Element where V: 'static, Render: Fn(&PopoverMenuItem, PopoverMenuItemState) -> Element, Dismiss: Fn(&mut V, &mut EventContext) + Clone + 'static,
entries.description: Build the complete unstyled interaction layer for one menu level. `render_item` owns all row geometry, colors, indicators, icons, and typography. Commands dispatch through the popover owner's ordinary typed-action path before `dismiss` runs.

entries.name: element_with_submenus
entries.type: pub fn element_with_submenus<V, Render, Dismiss, OpenSubmenu>( &self, cx: &mut ViewContext<'_, V>, id: impl Into<ElementId>, access: fn(&mut V) -> &mut PopoverMenu, root: Element, render_item: Render, dismiss: Dismiss, open_submenu: OpenSubmenu, ) -> Element where V: 'static, Render: Fn(&PopoverMenuItem, PopoverMenuItemState) -> Element, Dismiss: Fn(&mut V, &mut EventContext) + Clone + 'static, OpenSubmenu: Fn(&mut V, ElementId, PopoverMenu, &mut EventContext) + Clone + 'static,
entries.description: Build the complete unstyled interaction layer and expose submenu activation to the owner.

entries.name: element_with_submenus_and_hover
entries.type: pub fn element_with_submenus_and_hover<V, Render, Dismiss, OpenSubmenu, HoverItem>( &self, cx: &mut ViewContext<'_, V>, id: impl Into<ElementId>, access: fn(&mut V) -> &mut PopoverMenu, root: Element, render_item: Render, dismiss: Dismiss, open_submenu: OpenSubmenu, hover_item: HoverItem, ) -> Element where V: 'static, Render: Fn(&PopoverMenuItem, PopoverMenuItemState) -> Element, Dismiss: Fn(&mut V, &mut EventContext) + Clone + 'static, OpenSubmenu: Fn(&mut V, ElementId, PopoverMenu, &mut EventContext) + Clone + 'static, HoverItem: Fn(&mut V, usize, bool, &mut EventContext) + Clone + 'static,
entries.description: Build the complete unstyled interaction layer with owner-controlled hover behavior. This is the native-overflow adapter hook for delayed submenu opening and menu-aim safe corridors. `hover_item` receives entry and exit transitions for enabled interactive rows; it owns highlighting and any delayed work. The ordinary [`Self::element_with_submenus`] method preserves immediate-highlight behavior without allocating a timer.

sections.name: PopoverMenu::root_part
sections.signature: pub fn root_part(&self, id: impl Into<ElementId>, root: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate a caller-owned menu root with focus, keyboard, drag-region, and accessibility semantics without adding any appearance.

sections.name: PopoverMenu::item_part
sections.signature: pub fn item_part( &self, menu_id: impl Into<ElementId>, index: usize, item_root: Element, ) -> Option<Element>
sections.description: Decorate one caller-owned row with its exact menu-item semantics and stable derived ID.

sections.name: PopoverMenu::group_part
sections.description: Decorate an application-composed wrapper around a related item group.

sections.name: PopoverMenu::labeled_group_part
sections.signature: pub fn labeled_group_part( &self, menu_id: impl Into<ElementId>, label_index: usize, group: Element, ) -> Option<Element>
sections.description: Decorate a caller-composed item group and name it from one mounted group-label row. Returns `None` when `label_index` is not a group label. The caller owns visual nesting and layout; this helper adds only the native group role and mounted `labelled-by` relationship.

sections.name: PopoverMenu::checkbox_item_part
sections.signature: pub fn checkbox_item_part( &self, menu_id: impl Into<ElementId>, index: usize, item_root: Element, ) -> Option<Element>
sections.description: Decorate a checkbox row, Base UI's `Menu.CheckboxItem`. This is the kind-checked Base UI-named alias of [`Self::item_part`]: it returns `None` when `index` is not a checkbox row, so a composition that renders parts by name cannot silently mount the wrong semantics.

sections.name: PopoverMenu::radio_item_part
sections.signature: pub fn radio_item_part( &self, menu_id: impl Into<ElementId>, index: usize, item_root: Element, ) -> Option<Element>
sections.description: Decorate a radio row, Base UI's `Menu.RadioItem`.

sections.name: PopoverMenu::link_item_part
sections.signature: pub fn link_item_part( &self, menu_id: impl Into<ElementId>, index: usize, item_root: Element, ) -> Option<Element>
sections.description: Decorate a link row, Base UI's `Menu.LinkItem`.

sections.name: PopoverMenu::submenu_trigger_part
sections.signature: pub fn submenu_trigger_part( &self, menu_id: impl Into<ElementId>, index: usize, open: bool, item_root: Element, ) -> Option<Element>
sections.description: Decorate a submenu row, Base UI's `Menu.SubmenuTrigger`. The row already declares `has-popup` and `menuitem`; `open` adds the expanded state that Base UI publishes as `data-popup-open` while the child level is mounted.

sections.name: PopoverMenu::separator_part
sections.signature: pub fn separator_part( &self, menu_id: impl Into<ElementId>, index: usize, item_root: Element, ) -> Option<Element>
sections.description: Decorate a separator row, Base UI's `Menu.Separator`.

sections.name: PopoverMenu::group_label_part
sections.signature: pub fn group_label_part( &self, menu_id: impl Into<ElementId>, index: usize, item_root: Element, ) -> Option<Element>
sections.description: Decorate a group-label row, Base UI's `Menu.GroupLabel`.

sections.name: PopoverMenu::radio_group_part
sections.description: Decorate a caller-composed radio group, Base UI's `Menu.RadioGroup`. The group carries the native radio-group role so assistive technology reports "one of three" for its items. Membership itself stays in the model: every row built with [`PopoverMenuItem::radio`] names the group it belongs to, and [`Self::set_radio_value`] keeps exactly one of them checked.

sections.name: PopoverMenu::labeled_radio_group_part
sections.signature: pub fn labeled_radio_group_part( &self, menu_id: impl Into<ElementId>, label_index: usize, group: Element, ) -> Option<Element>
sections.description: Decorate a caller-composed radio group and name it from one mounted group-label row. Returns `None` when `label_index` is not a group label.

sections.name: PopoverMenu::checkbox_item_indicator_part
sections.description: Decorate a caller-owned checkbox indicator, Base UI's `Menu.CheckboxItemIndicator`. The indicator is decoration: the row it sits in already carries the checked state, so mounting a second announcement would make assistive technology read the value twice. Mount it only while the row is checked, exactly as Base UI does.

sections.name: PopoverMenu::radio_item_indicator_part
sections.description: Decorate a caller-owned radio indicator, Base UI's `Menu.RadioItemIndicator`.

entries.name: orientation
